title: Realization of a closed rational-point subgroup by its reduced closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Identify the rational points $G(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k,G)$ [def-weil-field-valued-points] with their underlying points and give them the subspace Zariski topology from $G$. Let $S\subseteq G(k)$ be a closed abstract subgroup: it contains $1$ and is stable under multiplication and inversion. Put $T=\overline S\subseteq |G|$, the topological closure, and let $H=T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow G$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then multiplication, identity and inverse of $G$ restrict to morphisms $H\times_kH\to H$, $\operatorname{Spec}k\to H$ and $H\to H$, making this inclusion a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $H(k)=S$. No affineness, smoothness or connectedness of $G$, and no perfectness of $k$, is assumed.

source.place: Section 1(c), Theorem 1.45 and its proof, printed p.19 (PDF p.31): the reduced closure of a closed subgroup of G(k) is an algebraic subgroup with those rational points. Algebraic group means separated finite-type group scheme; no affineness hypothesis. Reduced induced structure: Stacks Tag 01J3, schemes.tex, label lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

proof.text: By the reduced-induced-structure theorem, $j:H\hookrightarrow G$ is a closed immersion with $H$ reduced and image $T$. Each $s\in S\subseteq T$ lifts uniquely to $H(k)$ by the field-point factorization lemma. Conversely every $H(k)$-point has image in $T\cap G(k)$. The subspace-closure identity gives $T\cap G(k)=\overline S^{G(k)}=S$, since $S$ is closed in $G(k)$. Thus $H(k)=S$ via $j$, and these lifted points are dense in $|H|=T$.

source.place: Theorem 1.45, proof, printed p.19 (PDF p.31); density facts in Proposition 1.10 and Remark 1.14, printed pp.9-10.

proof.text: Apply the product lemma to the reduced $k$-scheme $H$ and its dense rational subset $S$, in both factors. It gives that $P=H\times_k H$ is reduced and that the paired $S$-points are dense in $|P|$. Here $H$ is finite type: locally in a finite affine finite-type cover of $G$, its coordinate rings are quotients of the coordinate rings of $G$, hence still generated by the images of their finitely many algebra generators.

source.place: Theorem 1.45, proof, printed p.19 (PDF p.31); density facts in Proposition 1.10 and Remark 1.14, printed pp.9-10.

proof.text: Put $u=m_G\circ(j\times_kj):P\to G$. The closed set $u^{-1}(T)$ contains every paired $(s,t)$, since $st\in S\subseteq T$. Its density from the preceding step gives $u(P)\subseteq T$. Likewise the closed set $(\mathrm{inv}_G\circ j)^{-1}(T)$ contains dense $S$, since $S^{-1}=S$, so it is all of $H$. The identity point lies in $T$ because $1\in S$. These arguments use continuity of scheme morphisms and closure, without identifying the scheme product topology with a product of topological spaces.

source.place: Theorem 1.45, proof, printed p.19 (PDF p.31); density facts in Proposition 1.10 and Remark 1.14, printed pp.9-10.

proof.text: Use the reduced-source factorization theorem on $u:P\to G$, $\mathrm{inv}_G\circ j:H\to G$, and $e_G:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$, with target closed subscheme $j:H\hookrightarrow G$. Their sources are reduced (the field spectrum has no nonzero nilpotents), and the preceding step supplies their image inclusions. Obtain $m_H$, $\mathrm{inv}_H$, $e_H$ with $j m_H=m_G(j\times j)$, $j\mathrm{inv}_H=\mathrm{inv}_G j$, $je_H=e_G$. They are over $k$, since their composites with $j$ are.

source.place: Theorem 1.45, proof, printed p.19 (PDF p.31); density facts in Proposition 1.10 and Remark 1.14, printed pp.9-10.

proof.text: A closed immersion cancels on morphisms: its point map is injective, and its structure-sheaf map is surjective, so two morphisms with equal composites have the same point map and the same sheaf map. Compose each associativity, left/right unit and left/right inverse diagram for the restricted maps with $j$; the defining factorization equations turn it into the corresponding diagram for $G$. Cancellation proves all the diagrams for $H$. It also gives injectivity of $H(R)\to G(R)$ for every $k$-algebra $R$. The restricted operations therefore make its image a subgroup, which is precisely a closed subgroup scheme; step 1 gives its required rational points.

I also read Milne iAG2017 Thm 1.45 and its proof (PDF p.31), and Def 1.9, Props 1.10, 1.11, 1.13, Cor 1.12 and Rem 1.14 (PDF pp.21-22). The item statement is unchanged and matches the existence part of 1.45 for separated finite-type groups over any field. Step 1 uses reduced-induced clause (2) and the field-point lift with K=k, and T∩G(k)=closure of S in G(k)=S. Step 2: H is reduced and finite type, and the lifted S is dense in H. Step 3 is a correct closure argument: u(s',t')=st lies in S, and it does not use the product topology. Step 4: the reduced-source factorization is applied to H×H (reduced by the new node), H and Spec k. Step 5: a closed immersion cancels (it is a monomorphism), which transfers the group diagrams and gives injectivity on R-points, as def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup requires. The two off-unit pbc tools are declared in tool_uses; I accept them. The new node is true over any field: evaluation at rational points separates elements on affine opens (1.10 (b)=>(c)); with q_i linearly independent over k, paired evaluations separate R⊗Q, which gives reducedness and density of the pairs. Finite type is not even needed. I checked the edge cases: empty schemes; Spec k[x]/(x^p-a) over an imperfect k, which has no rational points and so is excluded; μ_p; S={1}. The new node makes explicit the density of H(k)×H(k) in H×H that Milne uses without stating. It is strictly smaller than the item and not a restatement of an item clause.
